These fixtures execute unchanged faster-whisper 1.2.0 and 1.0.3 transcription methods. The respective `transcribe.py` SHA-256 values are `ecec022994e56d085351d5d4ff309db9017311680fc9171783b737139c739a6e` and `3356e6a48c801d97719cf0d16d785b8880e7cf2a5c642efb4434951c3cc485a5`. The external capture program is `/tmp/ezlocalai_whisper_transcription_oracle.py`. Repository runners are C++ and do not execute Python.

`../whisper_transcription_policy_{modern,legacy}.jsonl` each contains 140 segment-controller cases and 220 temperature-fallback cases. Only the encoder, decoder, alignment and language-detection engine boundary is substituted. The actual source controller, prompt construction, timestamp splitting, word heuristics and fallback selection execute unchanged. Each row records the complete engine call sequence as well as segments or the observed exception. Encoder calls include SHA-256 of the padded float32 features. Cases cover multiple windows and clips, previous context and prompt reset, initial text/token prompts, prefix/hotwords, multilingual changes, explicit empty suppression, no-speech handling, threshold boundaries, fallback exhaustion, word timestamps, anomalous alignments and maximum-token failures. The policy runners use the pinned compressed English and multilingual tokenizer files described in `../whisper_tokenizer_assets/README.md`.

`../whisper_transcription_model_{modern,legacy}.jsonl` each contains 16 complete transcriptions with actual CPU int8 CTranslate2 4.6.1 models and ONNX Runtime 1.24.1 VAD. The reference environment uses NumPy 1.26.4, tokenizers 0.22.1 and PyAV 12.3.0. Metadata records SHA-256 values for weights, configuration, tokenizer and vocabulary; all are checked before loading. Models remain external:

- `Systran/faster-whisper-tiny.en`, revision `0d3d19a32d3338f10357c0889762bd8d64bbdeba`; model SHA-256 `1a5afae06a4db91c975c9a9d78be5cc110ee4ea022ad57d55492e4550e936b2a`.
- `Systran/faster-whisper-tiny`, revision `d90ca5fe260221311c53c58e660288d3deb8d356`; model SHA-256 `dcb76c6586fc06cbdac6dd21f14cfd129cc4cdd9dce19bf4ffa62e59cbe6e6d1`.

VAD identities and configuration are shared with `../whisper_vad_model_cases.tsv`. Audio comes from the public JFK sample documented in `../whisper_kernel_assets/README.md`. Long audio repeats that sample three times with one-second silent gaps. Each `.f32z` contains zlib-compressed little-endian float32 samples; the row records its decompressed sample count. Cases include silence and empty input, language detection and forced language/task, word timestamps, clips, VAD, beam sizes 1/3, an initial prompt, a prefix and previous-context switches. They preserve profile-specific behavior, including legacy language detection reusing its final encoder output for the first transcription window and legacy empty automatic-language detection failing.

Tokens, text, segment IDs, seek positions, timestamp values and language decisions are compared exactly apart from a 1e-12 allowance for binary floating-point timestamp arithmetic. Model scores and probabilities use 1e-4 absolute tolerance, consistent with the existing kernel fixtures. The files above cover standard transcription. GPU execution, service lifecycle, diarization and arbitrary models/dependency versions remain outside these captures.

The batched fixtures execute the unchanged `BatchedInferencePipeline` from faster-whisper 1.2.0; version 1.0.3 does not provide this class. The external generator is `/tmp/ezlocalai_whisper_batched_oracle.py`, using the same tokenizer/audio/model assets and dependency versions as above.

- `../whisper_batched_policy.jsonl` has 300 policy cases and 342 generator invocations. Only the native engine boundary is substituted. Complete batch feature hashes, prompts, generation parameters, per-item language detection, alignment calls, segments, exceptions and persistent alignment state are captured. Cases cover batch sizes 1/2/3/8/0/-1, empty batches/results, timestamp splitting, word-boundary heuristics, prompt types, ignored fallback controls, first-temperature use, maximum-token failures and subsequent calls after an injected mid-batch failure. There are 321 recorded batch-generation calls, 116 alignment calls and a retained-state failure followed by recovery.
- `../whisper_batched_model_threads_{1,8}.jsonl` each has 25 complete actual-model cases. They include VAD defaults and overrides, clips, six-/ten-/thirty-second grouping, batch sizes 1/2/3/8, word timestamps, translation, language detection, multilingual batches, silence/empty input, null token suppression and invalid batch sizes. The test verifies the OpenBLAS thread count recorded in the fixture header before running. Set `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS` consistently for the reference capture and native test; CTest does so explicitly for both profiles. The final null-suppression case was appended with `/tmp/ezlocalai_whisper_batch_null_oracle.py`; the full generator also includes it for future recaptures.

Both standard and batched policy captures now include null suppression. Their engine-boundary traces normalize `None` to an empty token vector, matching CTranslate2 4.6.1's actual optional-vector binding. Floating generation parameters are likewise recorded after float32 conversion. The source controllers themselves are unchanged.

Thread count is observable for these int8 model cases. During verification, the reference's default eight-thread mel projection was initially compared with a one-thread native test. Features differed by at most 1.1920929e-7, but the first case's average log probability changed from -0.13064067363739013 to -0.12749824047088623. Matching eight-thread execution produced bitwise-identical encoder features and identical scores for that diagnostic case. Separate one-thread captures preserve the one-thread result rather than weakening the score tolerance. This is evidence that model/dependency/thread settings must match; it does not establish bitwise identity across arbitrary hardware or BLAS builds.
